## Result

- Skill: delivery-review.
- Review status: approved.
- Review ID: delivery-review-r5.
- Exact member: revised primary plan with M3 addendum and all-in-scope final checkpoint.
- Current upstream authority: design-review-r8, eight exact subjects.
- Material findings / required review-resolution: none.
- Next owner: Route for authorized M3 implementation; reviewer initializes or updates no work.
- Claim limits: allocation approval only; no current implementation, candidate, Code Review, Verify or PR readiness claim.

## Complete-plan assessment with M3

The plan retains M1/M2 safety, coherent authoring cutover and proof intent. M3 explicitly follows approval of the revised models/Delivery package and coordinates marker dispatch, diagnostics, seven living declarations, current boundary consumer, authoring guidance/skeleton and measured supported candidates. Earlier milestones' completed implementation is not overwritten or relabeled. The new milestone is justified by the requested observable document-format acceptance change, and remains within the original engineering responsibility.

M3's requirements cover DES-SR-09/11/12/16/19. It allocates accepted-marker proof; retired/unknown/missing/duplicate fail-closed proof; fenced parent/extracted-example tests; source/prose/model/selector checks; all supported archive generation/clean installs and metadata checks; and the installed authoring walkthrough against changed guidance. Invalid marker variants and one-live-parent-declaration checks give a meaningful oracle rather than snapshot changes alone. V3/V4/V6 and maintained selector checks preserve protective regression coverage; V5/V8 cover the newly measured candidate. Existing exact source allocation identifies the validator and resource/skeleton owners; no new service or test protocol is needed.

Because candidate identity changes, prior installed authoring and actual candidate public managed-replacement/recovery evidence cannot automatically remain current. M3 explicitly requires renewed walkthrough/candidate proof where those changed subjects matter and limits reuse to independently established unaffected basis. Helper/runtime logic can remain unchanged, but mocked/helper-only success cannot replace the new actual candidate path. New candidate generation uses a new empty task directory and measured metadata; no archive hand-edit, historical metadata rewrite or blanket release-only gate is allocated. Customer model edits remain separately authorized, and recovery restores the coherent document/validator/guidance/candidate set without runtime-format conversion.

The final checkpoint now explicitly requires all in-scope milestones M1–M3 and corrections. The earlier word both was corrected as an advisory consistency clarification because M3 already independently required its own review then fresh whole-change review/Verify; no missing gate or material finding was invented. Other M1/M2 references describe their retained behavior/proof scope, not permission to skip M3. The final complete-change assessment and distinct Verify still precede updating the existing PR.

## Evidence and limits

Independent inspection of current validator/resource dispatch shows the prospective marker is not implemented; its expected rejection is not hidden as a passing test or accepted implementation defect. The parent/example grammar feasibility check described in r8 supports the chosen unchanged structure but is not actual new-marker proof. Delivery acceptance still requires that actual proof, rebuilt installed methods and current candidate recovery evidence. The pure-function example is illustrative; no label-normalization runtime implementation or component test suite is added to scope.

Prior plan/review subjects remain historical; this judgment attaches to the revised plan identity and current r8 package. The existing failed historical installer prose limitation persists, with no blanket waiver. No work entries, lifecycle route, governed content or historical approval is changed by this review.

Concrete independent nonauthor /root/independent_design_review assessed the user-requested marker rename and illustrative example plus complete affected Design and Delivery packages. Primary-agent authored all governed model/plan changes; reviewer performed read-only semantic/structural feasibility checks and authored only these reviews. Passing author checks and prior approvals do not substitute for this assessment.
